reason: This passage (Exodus 17:1-7, the water from the rock at Rephidim) describes social roles and hierarchy—Moses as leader, elders as witnesses to God's miraculous provision—but makes no claim about inherent superiority. The text focuses on God's response to the people's thirst and lack of faith, not on any assertion that the elite are inherently better. While elders are mentioned as witnesses (לְעֵינֵי זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל), their role is functional (bearing witness to the miracle), not a statement of their inherent superiority over the common people (הָעָם).
